caption: : Self-reflection SFT data statistic

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of samples across different reasoning categories within the self-reflection supervised fine-tuning (SFT) dataset. The horizontal axis represents the categorical labels of reasoning types, listed from left to right as “Mathematical Reasoning,” “General Reasoning,” “Natural Scene Reasoning,” “Physical Reasoning,” “Logical Puzzle Reasoning,” and “Chemical Reasoning,” arranged in the order they appear on the chart. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of Samples” and employs a logarithmic scale ranging from 10² to 10⁴, with tick marks and grid lines indicating the logarithmic intervals. Each bar corresponds to one reasoning category and is annotated with its exact sample count: “Mathematical Reasoning” has 7025 samples, “General Reasoning” has 1709, “Natural Scene Reasoning” has 413, “Physical Reasoning” has 232, “Logical Puzzle Reasoning” has 91, and “Chemical Reasoning” has 49. The bars are presented in a single group, with each bar standing independently to represent the count for its respective category. There is no visual indication of grouping or stacking, and the bars are not sorted by height; they are displayed in the sequence defined by the horizontal axis labels. The bars are uniformly colored in light blue and are not visually distinguished by any additional formatting such as shading, bolding, or outlines.

The bars are arranged in descending order of sample count from left to right, and there are no visual elements such as shading, bolding, or annotations used to emphasize any particular bar.
